I re-swept the history myself: 74 commits carry src/ at 56c4e0f (73 at 6237858, so their count was exact), and K16 reports exactly one site ever, fab.cull_gate, at the 34 trees since d8afb7b and nowhere else; the 39/37/2 breakdown of the silent trees is right to the commit (f046b25 and 38a5d7e, four Gates each, examining three). I re-counted the population from scratch rather than reading their report line: 114 Gate constructions = 0 no-pair + 79 unresolved + 27 descriptive + 8 examined, and the 8 are the 8 they name. '25 thresholds are a bare string and 23 an f-string' -> 25 and 23. 'sixteen pass a bare None for one half' -> 16. K15's '15 computed, 13 judged, 2 outside' -> 15/13/2, and the 2 are opt.lr.warmup and opt.lr.min_frac exactly as filed. The K15 two-sided bool() unwrap is a real recovered detection: with it one-sided, my own both-sides plants go UNDETECTED. The O13 widening is a true superset at every one of the 74 trees (I dumped both examined sets per tree; it never shrinks), it adds three findings at four trees and they are all one real false attribution (assemble.py quoting 'are registered' where tok/levers.py:96 says 'were registered'), and h_docs' end-anchored-only form does drop spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_windows -- 6 examined against 7. Their REFUTED verdict on it is right.
WHAT DOES NOT. (1) THE OPERATOR CENSUS IS MISCOUNTED. tests/test_contract.py:4470-4472 says '25 of the resolved verdicts are `>`, 2 `==`, 2 `is not`, 1 `<`, 1 `!=`'. The total, 31, is right and is the size of exactly one population in this tree -- Gates with exactly one LIVE clause -- but that population is 25 `>`, 2 `<`, 2 `==`, 2 `is not` and ZERO `!=`, identically at 6237858 and at 56c4e0f. The tree's only `!=` is src/opt/api.py:1643 opt.lr.sched, whose clause is its own `reachable=` and is subtracted, so it can never reach the direction question; and the second `<`, src/fabric/api.py fab.depth_curriculum, was counted as it. The consequence clause is wrong with it: on the examined set the naive 'fired implies value >= threshold' rule would falsely report ONE gate (data.splice_window), not two. The POSITION -- do not judge direction -- survives on that one gate. (2) 'EVERY MECHANISM IS SEEN TO FAIL' IS FALSE. I mutated 17 mechanisms one at a time in a fresh subprocess against a full mirror. Eleven are pinned. SIX are pinned by NOTHING in all 77 cases, and FIVE of those six are load-bearing -- I wrote a plant for each and it goes red: the single-assignment Name unfold, the bool() unwrap inside _k16_deciding_predicate, the round/int/float/abs unwrap, the UNORDERED operand key, and the structured descent in _k16_clauses. Delete any one and the whole suite stays green while K16 silently loses a detection or gains a false alarm. By this repository's own rule -- 'an exemption nothing can trip is the same defect as a guard nothing can trip', O11's docstring -- that is a defect. (3) K16'S EMPTY-ARM GUARANTEE IS NARROWER THAN ITS CASE TITLE. 'a reason that is EMPTY on the arm the verdict prints on does not exempt the gate' holds only when `reachable=` is passed, because that is the only thing _k15_live_reason can resolve the arm against. With no `reachable=`, a reason of `('' if C else '')` -- empty on EVERY arm, so Gate.line prints the verdict word and the pair and nothing else on every configuration -- exempts the Gate. I planted it: rc=0. And this is not hypothetical: the ONE gate K16 exempts in this tree today, the repaired fab.cull_gate, is exempted through exactly that path, its arm chosen by `not cull_open and n0 <= 2`. I swept that gate's line over 15 real assemblies including NEGATIVE ZERO and slots=0 and its empty arm IS correct -- but K16 did not establish that and cannot.
ITEM 7, THE RED: NOT APPLICABLE ANY MORE, AND I SAY SO WITH THE PROOF RATHER THAN DROPPING IT. Both of j_k16's unfinished repairs landed in 56c4e0f. The suite is GREEN: ownership 13+43, contract 16+77, census 8, assemble 9, couplings 4, fabric 9, derive 575, 0 failing everywhere. Their suite_after is STALE, correctly so.
ITEM 4, THE LEVER SWEEP: fab.cull_gate prints a self-consistent line on all 15 configurations I built, including FAB_PRESSURE=-0.0 at three widths and FAB_SLOTS=0. No sentence contradicts its own arithmetic.

findings.symbol: tests/test_contract.py::check_k16_verdicts_follow_their_printed_pair -- a conditional reason that is EMPTY on the arm that prints still exempts, unless `reachable=` decides the arm
findings.detail: AN UNDISCLOSED HOLE THAT THE ONE GATE K16 EXEMPTS IN THIS TREE GOES THROUGH. The check's self-test case is titled 'a reason that is EMPTY on the arm the verdict prints on does not exempt the gate', and the exemption is coded as: if the reason is an ast.IfExp AND `reachable=` is present, ask _k15_live_reason which arm prints and test THAT arm for emptiness; otherwise treat any non-Constant reason as a reason. So the guarantee holds only where `reachable=` is passed, which is the one shape _k15_live_reason can resolve an arm against. WITH NO `reachable=`, A REASON OF `('' if C else '')` -- empty on EVERY arm, so spine/gate.py::Gate.line prints the verdict word, the pair and nothing else on every configuration -- EXEMPTS THE GATE. I planted it: rc=0, silent. AND IT IS LIVE. The one Gate K16 exempts today is src/fabric/api.py:657 fab.cull_gate, whose repaired reason is a nested ternary whose arms are chosen by `not cull_open and n0 <= 2` and by a rounding test -- neither is `reachable=`, which that Gate does not pass -- and whose third arm is `""`. K16 accepts it without ever asking whether the empty arm is reachable. I established by running it that the empty arm IS correct there (see the lever sweep below), but the check did not and cannot. This is an UNDER-report, so nothing false is being claimed -- but the block's 'WHAT IT LEAVES OUT' list, which exists precisely to put the residue on the report rather than in a docstring, does not name it, and neither does the report line. TIGHTENING IT IS NOT THE FIX: any rule that treats an unresolvable-arm reason as no reason reports fab.cull_gate, which is correct today, and that is crying wolf. The fix is disclosure plus a count.

MY ANSWER IS (a), WITH A QUALIFICATION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE LETTER. What I found on these two files this round is three real things -- a miscounted census, a false universal about the self-test, and an undisclosed hole in the newest check that the one gate it exempts goes through. None of them is a wrong CHECK. All three are claims ABOUT a check: a count beside a rule, a universal about what the rule's own tests pin, and an omission from the rule's own residue list. That is a different class from round one's nine highs, and it is a different class from 'churn' too, because the number of them is falling and none of them was introduced by a fix to another one.
THE EVIDENCE FOR (a) RATHER THAN (c). The undisclosed hole is not cosmetic: five self-test mechanisms can be deleted today with the entire suite staying green, and two of those deletions turn K16 into a false-alarm generator rather than merely a quieter check. This repository's own stated rule -- 'an exemption nothing can trip is the same defect as a guard nothing can trip' -- classifies that as a defect, and it was not found by the round that shipped the check even though that round explicitly went looking ('EVERY MECHANISM IS SEEN TO FAIL'). A verifier who reads the report and re-runs its repros finds nothing; a verifier who mutates the code finds five. That gap is a reason to keep auditing at least one more round, on the mutation axis specifically.
THE EVIDENCE FOR (c) RATHER THAN (a), WHICH IS THE STRONGEST CASE AGAINST MY OWN ANSWER, and I think it is genuinely strong. Every LOAD-BEARING claim reproduced. I planted 29 constructs designed to break K16 and 0 broke it. I swept 74 trees for K16 and 74 for the widened O13 and found exactly the calibration claimed -- one true instance, zero false alarms, a true superset at every tree. I re-counted eleven published numbers from scratch (114, 0/79/27/8, 25 bare-string and 23 f-string thresholds, 16 half-None gates, 15/13/2, 73 and 74 trees, 37+2 silent trees, 0/2/1 rule-5 populations, 3->7 examined, 6 under the end-anchored form, 151/166 at 6237858) and TEN of the eleven were exact to the unit. The one that was not is a decorative sub-breakdown whose total was right and whose conclusion survives. Every line number j_k16 gave was correct at the commit they named it at. Both hand-off repairs landed and the suite is green with no check narrowed. On a per-finding basis the severity really has collapsed: the highest thing I can honestly call a live defect is a missing test case, not a wrong answer.
WHAT I WOULD TELL THE OWNER. The checks on this surface are sound; what is not yet sound is the SECOND-ORDER layer -- the prose, counts and universals that describe them. Three consecutive rounds have now shipped a miscount inside a correction to a miscount, and this round did it again in the census beside the newest rule. That is a real cost but it is a bounded and cheap one, and it does not block anything: no miscounted sentence in either of these files can make a check answer wrong. THE SIX ENTRY POINTS ARE THE HIGHER-VALUE WORK. I would take the five self-test cases in this report (they are written and measured; adding them is mechanical), take the three prose repairs, and then STOP auditing this surface and go build compose(), auditing it as it is written rather than after. If the owner wants one more pass here, make it a MUTATION pass over all sixteen K checks and thirteen O checks rather than another read-through -- that is the axis that found something this round, and the axis that seven read-throughs did not.
